module.purpose: NestJS controller exposing email verification endpoints under /v2/atoms. It routes requests for sending verification codes, checking whether verification is required, verifying codes (authenticated and unauthenticated), and listing/adding verified emails, delegating all logic to VerificationAtomsService.
module.summary: This file defines AtomsVerificationController, a versioned NestJS REST controller mounted at /v2/atoms and tagged for Atoms verification endpoints (excluded from generated docs). It delegates to VerificationAtomsService. Endpoints: POST /verification/email/send-code sends a verification code, rate-limited to 3 requests per minute via Throttle; GET /verification/email/check determines if email verification is required by comparing an email with the user session email; POST /verification/email/verify-code verifies a code without authentication, while POST /verification/email/verify-code-authenticated performs the same verification guarded by ApiAuthGuard with the current user injected via GetUser; GET /emails/verified-emails lists a user's (or team's) verified emails and POST /emails/verified-emails adds a verified email, both guarded by ApiAuthGuard. All responses wrap results in ApiResponse payloads with SUCCESS_STATUS and return HTTP 200.
module.businessContext: Serves the Cal.com platform's booking atoms, ensuring users verify secondary email addresses before use. If it fails, users cannot confirm emails or manage verified addresses, potentially allowing unverified emails in scheduling flows.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Verification code send succeeds and is not skipped
moduleContractTests.when: POST /v2/atoms/verification/email/send-code with body { email, username, language, isVerifyingEmail }
moduleContractTests.then: 200 response with { data: { sent: true }, status: SUCCESS_STATUS }

moduleContractTests.rationale: Skipped sends must not be reported as sent.

moduleContractTests.then: the 4th request is throttled (limit 3, ttl 60000, blockDuration 60000)

moduleContractTests.scenario: Checking whether email verification is required

moduleContractTests.then: 200 with { data: { verified: true }, status: SUCCESS_STATUS }

moduleContractTests.scenario: Authenticated code verification with a valid session
moduleContractTests.then: service called as verifyEmailCodeAuthenticated(user, { email, code }) and result wrapped in { data: { verified }, status: SUCCESS_STATUS }
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins user context propagation to service.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Anonymous request to authenticated verify endpoint
Listing verified emails with optional teamId query
moduleContractTests.then: service receives teamId: 42 (number) and response is { data: verifiedEmails, status: SUCCESS_STATUS }

moduleContractTests.scenario: Adding a verified email for the authenticated user
given: authenticated user with id and email
moduleContractTests.then: service called with { userId: user.id, existingPrimaryEmail: user.email, email: body.email }; response { data: { emailVerified }, status: SUCCESS_STATUS }
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins userId/existingPrimaryEmail sourced from session, not body.
